For fixed weights in eval mode, cache catalog-wide candidate vectors LN(e_i) and W_i LN(e_i), preserving each LayerNorm’s parameters and each projection’s bias. Per sequence and target position, cache W_h LN(h), the five history vectors and mask, and any candidate-independent attention keys. If weighted_history = Σα_jv_j, linearity also permits caching W_vv_j and summing those projections; add W_v’s bias once after aggregation. These are algebraic deductions, assuming feature-only normalization as specified by [PyTorch LayerNorm](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/generated/torch.nn.functional.layer_norm.html). Candidate-dependent queries, attention weights, aggregated histories and final normalized outputs still require candidate-specific computation. LayerNorm cannot move through the weighted sum. Floating-point reassociation can introduce small differences, so algebraic equivalence does not guarantee bitwise equality.

Make context an explicit object passed to scoring: sequence features, aligned history windows, masks, target positions, and model/category identity. Avoid mutable “last sequence” state: interleaved calls otherwise silently reuse another batch’s history. When selecting positions, slice features, windows and masks together; for final-position inference, construct the window at the actual target position, respecting padding and causal alignment. Candidate chunks must reuse the same context and gather matching candidate IDs from the catalog cache. Normalize attention over the five history slots, never the candidate chunk; [PyTorch softmax](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/generated/torch.nn.functional.softmax.html) normalizes along its specified dimension. Invalidate caches after weight, device or dtype changes. Verify cached versus uncached scores across batched users, interleaved contexts, position slices and multiple chunk sizes, including padding edge cases. Caching is feasible; integration difficulty depends on making these ownership and alignment guarantees explicit.
